scope: Fixed body support roles for ordinary two-arm, two-leg humanoids; character-specific hair and clothing chains are fitted after these roles and before final weight refinement.

requiredBonesPerSide.name: WB_Physics_Breast_{side}
requiredBonesPerSide.placement: Fit a same-side tissue center and outward rest endpoint from the original surface; keep the medial boundary and attachment to the torso fixed. Never use global left/right alone to classify vertices. All humanoids retain this role, even with subtle influence.

requiredBonesPerSide.name: WB_Physics_Glute_{side}
requiredBonesPerSide.placement: Fit a same-side tissue center and outward rest endpoint from the original surface; keep the medial boundary and attachment to the torso fixed. Never use global left/right alone to classify vertices. All humanoids retain this role, even with subtle influence.

rules: All 26 fixed body support roles are required: thirteen per side. Reuse a verified equivalent using runtime.supportBones[canonicalRole]=actualBoneName, never duplicate it. An anatomical donor bone is not a support-role equivalent.
Transfer the full donor skeleton and starting weights to the connected ORIGINAL first; add fixed body bones, then complete character-specific hair/clothing chains; only then refine all weight maps.
Keep every donor bone, parent and rest joint position. Added bones are branches. An existing equivalent must satisfy the required parent without reparenting the donor; otherwise report the conflict.

Twist fractions are 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75 along each upper arm, forearm and thigh. Swing-following helpers share the anatomical pivot; weights form overlapping longitudinal zones, not three identical full-limb masks. Target axes are measured in target REST LOCAL space.
Resolve Shoulder to Chest/UpperChest/Spine only when that donor role is absent; resolve Chest to UpperChest/Spine when absent. Record the resolved attachment. Do not invent anatomical bones.
Measure signed joint flexion and convex direction from a test bend; fit the existing elbow/knee volume recipe in the correct parent/source local frames. Do not use new shape keys.

Secondary bones are explicitly declared in runtime.secondary with kind, bones in parent-to-child order, attachment, original mesh names, region description and simulated:false. They inherit parent motion in the preview; this is not a PhysBones simulation.
Do not add Blender-only behavior that the viewer cannot reproduce. Every twist and volume helper needs its supported runtime recipe. Physics-ready bones must not have fake zero-motion twist recipes.
Never delete, merge or renumber source vertices or change UVs, materials, hair normals or approved morphs while building the rig.

weightCleanup.crossLimb: Identify limb ownership from corresponding donor parts, anatomy and mesh connectivity, not x-sign or nearest joint alone. In unambiguous limbs remove opposite-leg/opposite-arm influences including their auxiliaries and redistribute to allowed same-side bones. Keep a deliberate central pelvis/crotch transition and center-spanning garments. Test each side alone and measure unintended opposite-side displacement.
weightCleanup.shoulders: Smooth the transition locally across upper arm, shoulder and chest, retaining chest/torso support in the axilla. Test arm elevation at 0, 45, 90 and 120 degrees and do not globally smooth unrelated face, hair, hand or clothing regions.
weightCleanup.helpers: Redistribute existing regional influence to the specified helpers using a smooth longitudinal falloff for twist branches and a local convex-joint falloff for volume helpers. Keep actual weighted vertices for each helper.
weightCleanup.smoothRegions: Use connected-surface neighborhoods and semantic masks. Smooth shoulder/axilla/chest, elbow, hip/groin/glute attachment, knee and ankle transitions locally. Use overlapping smooth ramps for twist zones, protected attachment bands for tissue and root-to-tip blends for chains. Preserve intentional creases and different layers; never blur weights by Euclidean proximity across legs, fingers, loose fabric or hair.
weightCleanup.protectedRegions: Preserve face pieces as a coordinated Head attachment in this body stage. Fingers have individual ownership with local knuckle blends; soles and rigid accessories retain coherent support. Breast and glute influence tapers to zero at medial and torso attachment boundaries; avoid dragging opposite tissue, ribs, pelvis or shoulders.
weightCleanup.budget: Prune to four influences only after redistribution, using regional ownership and preserving the principal supporting bone; normalize after each cleanup pass. Recheck deformation after pruning. Source UV duplicates must have identical named-bone weights.
weightCleanup.evidence: Provide weightAudit in report.json with before/after metrics, region ownership decisions, paired one-side pose checks, graded shoulder/elbow/knee/twist poses and relative paths to evidence. A structural pass is not a claim of professional artistic quality.

deferred: Face rig, expressions and visemes (separate section)
Physics simulation/colliders and Unity/VRChat destination setup
acceptance: All 26 fixed roles present exactly once and actually weighted
Twist/volume recipes match fixed profile and measured local frames
Hair/clothing inventory complete with fitted chains or justified body-following regions
No cross-limb movement outside intentional central transitions
Normalized weights, maximum four influences, no unweighted vertices or conflicting UV-seam weights
Rest geometry, source identities, UVs, textures, normals and donor hierarchy/joints preserved
Evidence reviewed for both sides, joints, tissue attachments and secondary chains; unresolved defects reported

secondaryChains.hair: Inspect scalp attachments, bangs, side locks, back masses and ponytails. Add independent chains only for masses that should move independently; roots follow Head. Trace each chain through its own volume; protect scalp and face. Close or overlapping locks are not automatic neighbors. Do not copy a fixed hairstyle.
secondaryChains.clothing: Classify fitted cloth, loose hems/panels, skirts, straps and rigid accessories. Fitted cloth follows the underlying body; loose regions receive chains anchored to the relevant torso/pelvis/limb. A skirt may need radial chains and body/chain blending near the waistband; do not bind the entire skirt independently to the nearest leg. Rigid buckles must not be globally smoothed.
secondaryChains.inventory: Report every original hair/clothing mesh or named subregion with decision chain or follows-body and reason. No hair or loose garment may be silently skipped. Record actual chain names and attachment bones. Keep bones within their assigned geometry region.
secondaryChains.limits: Fit chain density to curvature and deformation need, not every strand/triangle. Maximum 128 declared secondary chains and 256 secondary bones; if exceeded, report rather than silently truncate.
secondaryChains.simulation: Create the bones and weights now. PhysBones components, colliders, runtime limits and collision groups are configured and tested in the later destination stage.
